newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Iran said planning refinery in the Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Iran said planning refinery in the Philippines.

text.p: The Iranian government is firming up plans to put up an oil refinery project in the southern Philippines with a Filipino partner, a Philippine government official said on Tuesday.

Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development chairman Nur Misuari told a news conference the project with initial production capacity of 150,000 barrels of oil per day is expected to start construction in November this year.
"The project will have an initial investment of $150 million but we are looking at more investments in the downstream industries," he said.

Misuari, who is leaving for Tehran to finalise the agreement, said four other similar projects may also be put up by foreign investors in the southern island of Mindanao. He however declined to identify the investors.
Misuari was appointed head of the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development, an interim body meant to pave the way for an autonomous region in the southern Philippines.

Misuari was head of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) which for years fought a violent war for a separate Islamic state but later agreed to an autonomous region within the mainly Catholic Philippines.
Since the signing of last year's peace pact with Manila, MNLF rebels have laid down their arms.
